title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 1st District
area: Tulsa County and part of Rogers County, including the city of Tulsa

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Kevin Hern is running for U.S. Senate rather than seeking re-election. Mark Tedford advanced unopposed after the Republican primary runoff was canceled; John Croisant advanced unopposed after the Democratic primary was canceled.

candidates.name: Mark Tedford
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced after the Republican primary runoff was canceled
candidates.currentRole: Member, Oklahoma House of Representatives, District 69 (Tulsa)

priorities.text: "An economy that works" — rebuilding domestic supply chains and manufacturing and pursuing energy independence.
priorities.quote: Reindustrialization is not only possible but essential for national security. America must rebuild critical supply chains and stop relying on foreign adversaries for pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and rare earth minerals.

priorities.text: Government accountability — reducing spending and addressing what he describes as fraud and abuse in programs like Medicaid and SNAP.
priorities.quote: Programs like Medicaid and SNAP were created to help those in need, but lax standards, fraud, and abuse have expanded dependency and strained resources.

priorities.text: Describes his campaign as guided by "American Values" including capitalism and what he calls Western Judeo-Christian founding principles.

positions.summary: His campaign website lists strict enforcement of immigration laws and support for deporting people it calls criminal aliens among his issues.
His campaign website lists protecting the unborn among his priorities under faith, family and freedom.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (tedfordforcongress.com) read in full; it lists issues as short bullets without detailed policy text. No stated position found on healthcare coverage, minimum wage, tariffs, or other listed topics. Tedford's campaign website was not located.

statements.context: On his campaign website, under rebuilding the economy

candidates.name: John Croisant
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced after the Democratic primary was canceled
candidates.currentRole: Member, Tulsa Public Schools Board of Education, District 5 (since 2020)

priorities.text: Addressing the affordability crisis, citing rising costs of healthcare, housing and childcare for working-class Oklahomans.
priorities.quote: The rising costs of healthcare, housing, childcare and other essentials are skyrocketing at a pace that working class Oklahomans cannot keep up with.

priorities.text: Improving education outcomes and opposing the elimination of the U.S. Department of Education.
priorities.quote: First, ensuring the Department of Education is not shut down. Second, I will hold Dept. of Ed. accountable for the outcomes of our students.

priorities.text: Protecting funding for healthcare, housing, childcare, education, infrastructure and job training programs.

positions.summary: His campaign site supports expanding access through Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies or a broader universal coverage model, and says he will fight to repeal recent federal Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: I support expanding access through Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies, or a broader universal coverage model.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for redirecting ICE resources toward immigration courts to clear the backlog, while also supporting a secure border and accountability for people breaking the law.
positions.quote: We should redirect ICE resources toward immigration courts to clear the backlog and make the system more efficient.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for stopping the flow of public money to private schools with no strings attached.
positions.quote: stopping the flow of public money to private schools with no strings attached.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
